slots.hypothesis: day_cov(Vwap,Ret) ≈ (P̄/M)(Q/2 − Rδ): price level × realized variance (a control proxy, trap 3) mixed with how late in the day the move happened (−Rδ). The new periphery removes the proxy part and keeps only the timing term. It divides by day_mean(Vwap)·day_var(Ret) or day_std·day_std, compares stocks only within deciles of today's variance, 20-day volatility or price level, adds a signed version (close vs the time-weighted average price), and smooths over 5/10/20 days or takes the 20-day innovation. No LimitWidth and no convex transforms; the only peripheries seen before are {add} (adding a board constant) and {add, ts_min}. Mechanism: under A-share T+1, late-day moves are mostly noise-driven price pressure that reverses in the next session (Chu-Gu-Zhou 2019). 14 seeds.

Up/down asymmetry of the minute-return distribution, read as lottery or attention-driven retail buying (Barberis-Huang 2008; Amaya et al. 2015 intraday realized skewness; Bali et al. 2011 MAX). Every seed is a scale-free ratio, so none rewrites a control: day_skew(Ret), the upside semivariance share, right-tail ES ratio and tail asymmetry, (max+min)/std, the standardized return in the heaviest-volume minutes, the tick-rule volume imbalance and the imbalance left after removing the price path's own. Multi-day versions use cross_mean 5/20, cross_max 20 and a rank within 20-day-volatility buckets. Batch 1 had no third-moment or volume-asymmetry structure. 15 seeds.
